text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A man died and two were injured in an explosion in Tallinn. Last autumn an explosion in the same building injured three women.

- President Lennart Meri appointed Tallinn mayor Robert Lepikson as interior minister. The Postimees newspaper predicted that former interior minister Riivo Sinijarv will become Estonian Ambassador to Tokyo.
- No Estonians were refused entry by officials in Helsinki on the first day of visa-free travel, an Estonian diplomat said.
- Teachers in Tartu and Parnu will join the May 12 strike of teachers in Tallinn.
- Trade unions demanded a 1,200-kroon minimum wage and the establishment of a guarantee fund at a May 1 rally in which 400-500 people took part.
- The national defence council met Wednesday to discuss how to implement a mobilisation system in Estonia.
- The director of shipping company Inreko Laeva said they would start bankruptcy proceedings against another shipping firm, Hansatee, if the latter does not repay a 80 million kroon debt.
